title: An extension obtained by adjoining a root of the prepared polynomial is Galois and falls into one of four cases according to the valuation of the parameter
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a discrete valuation ring A of mixed characteristic (0, p) containing a primitive p-th root of 1, the polynomial P of the preparation lemma, and an element xi of the fraction field K, and considers the extension L obtained by adjoining a root of P(z) = xi; it asserts that L/K is Galois and that exactly one of four cases occurs — L = K; L/K unramified with respect to A of degree p; L/K totally ramified of ramification index p; or the integral closure B is a discrete valuation ring with A in B weakly unramified and a purely inseparable residue extension of degree p — and then, with pi a uniformizer of A, asserts three implications (A), (B) and (C) locating the case according to the shape of xi (source lines 35016-35042). The proof rewrites the adjunction of a root of P(z) = xi as the adjunction of a root of y^p = w^p (1 + xi), notes that K contains a primitive p-th root of 1 so the extension is Galois of order dividing p by Kummer theory, and reads the case list off the ramification discussion (proof lines 35045-35051). Case (A) is settled by observing that A -> A[x]/(P(x) - xi) is then a finite etale ring extension, so only cases (1) and (2) can occur (proof lines 35054-35055). Case (B) is settled by a valuation count: writing xi = pi^{-n} a with p not dividing n and letting B be the integral closure with C = B_m, one has p ord_C(z) = -n ord_C(pi), so the ramification index of A in C is divisible by p, hence equals p, and B = C (proof lines 35058-35063). Case (C) is the substantive one: writing k = n/p the proof rewrites the defining equation in the displayed form with (pi^k z) as the new variable, and concludes from the fact that A[y]/(y^p - pi^{n-k} y - sum a_i pi^{n-ik} y^i - a) is a discrete valuation ring weakly unramified over A (proof lines 35066-35071). The non-routine content is the Kummer rewriting together with the explicit discrete valuation ring in case (C).
